hero.heading: Every app on HTTPS, every packet accounted for.
hero.lead: Bridges, VLANs and firewalling with eBPF. Every app gets a local name with a valid certificate, and remote access works without opening ports.

items.title: Networks
items.body: Linux bridges, VLANs and bonds managed over netlink, for IPv4 and IPv6.

items.title: DHCP and IPAM
items.body: Addresses for VMs and apps, with reservations and no conflicts.

items.title: eBPF policy
items.body: Per-workload firewall rules enforced in the kernel with Aya.

items.title: Flow logs
items.body: See which app talked to what, and what was blocked, with metrics per workload.

items.title: Host firewall
items.body: nftables protects the host itself before anything else starts.

items.title: Ingress and TLS
items.body: Caddy as reverse proxy, with three certificate modes.

items.title: Local names
items.body: Every app gets <name>.crust.internal, announced with mDNS on your LAN.

items.title: Remote access
items.body: NetBird first; Tailscale or Headscale as an option. No port forwarding.

items.title: Node links
items.body: WireGuard between nodes, iroh across sites.

how.heading: From packet to app, in four layers.
how.lead: Each layer is a resource in the API, so a firewall rule is as easy to review as a VM.

steps.title: Host
steps.body: nftables locks down the host; only the API, ingress and what you allow are open.

steps.title: Networks
steps.body: Bridges and VLANs connect VMs and apps, with DHCP and IPAM.

steps.title: Policy
steps.body: eBPF programs enforce per-workload rules and record flows.

steps.title: Ingress
steps.body: Caddy terminates TLS and routes names to apps.

rows: Local CA, Let's Encrypt (HTTP-01 or DNS-01), bring your own
Local CA, Let's Encrypt, your own certificate

ask.body: "Why can't Jellyfin reach my NAS?" The assistant reads flow logs and policy, finds the rule that blocks it, and proposes a fix you confirm.

faq.title: Do I need my own domain?
faq.body: No. Apps get names under crust.internal with the local CA. Add your own domain when you want public HTTPS.

faq.title: How do devices trust the local CA?
faq.body: Install the root certificate once per device; the setup wizard shows a QR code and links per OS.

faq.title: Why eBPF and not just iptables?
faq.body: eBPF gives per-app policy and flow data with low overhead. nftables still guards the host.

faq.title: Do I have to open ports?
faq.body: No. Remote access goes through NetBird or Tailscale.
